newsitem.title: FRANCE: FSU union slams civil service pay talks delays.
newsitem.headline: FSU union slams civil service pay talks delays.

text.p: France's big FSU trade union accused the government on Thursday of dragging its heels after putting off civil service pay talks slated for Monday and called other unions to unite in the campaign on pay and jobs.
A civil service ministry spokesman confirmed that talks had been postponed, probably to early February, but said the delay was because of agenda complications and nothing else.

"The civil service minister has decided to postpone meetings with civil service unions...to present government proposals," the FSU, the largest union among teachers and the rest of the five million central administration's civil servants, said.
"The margin which the government is giving itself looks so narrow that it can only confirm the impasse on 1996 pay and the continuing erosion of purchasing power," it said in a statement.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe gave the go-ahead in December for the opening of pay talks with civil service minister Dominique Perben after a wage freeze in 1996 but unions are fighting for 1996 pay to be included in the negotiations.
